- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
TLDR: For the fused reduce-scatter + RMSNorm kernel, this PR fixes a masking bug that causes wrong outputs, whereas for the non-fused AGV/RSV kernels in `variable_collectives.py` that are used more frequently, this just fixes a bug that causes duplicate communication of values rather than wrong outputs.

This PR does two things:
1.) First, it fixes a masking bug which causes a block to leak into another block's token, causing duplicate communication in the non-fused AGV/RSV kernels in `variable_collectives.py`, and causing wrong outputs in the fused reduce-scatter + RMSNorm kernel in the `fused_collectives.py` file. Currently, the channel-masking code only handles the case when `BLOCK_SIZE > numel_per_token` due to power-of-2 padding. However, in the specific case that `numel_per_token` is not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE and `numel_per_token > BLOCK_SIZE`, in the final window we have a thread array with IDs `[channel_offset, channel_offset + BLOCK_SIZE)`, where `channel_offset + BLOCK_SIZE` is greater than `numel_per_token`. This causes the current block to launch collectives on the channel's of the next token-row, which is already handled by another block, so there is duplicate communication. This special case only arises when `BLOCK_SIZE` is maxed out at 1024 and when the model's hidden size is > 8192 for BF16 values.
2.) Second, it removes the `token_mask` which is actually just redundant since the outer-loop already enforces the range of the `token_offset` counter to be `[pid, local_tokens)`, so we will never cross the boundary of the rank's input buffer. Also I removed `local_numel` since that is no longer used after these changes.

- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests

- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"
